CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. What You’ll Do
Applications Engineering, part of CoreWeave’s Data Infrastructure organization, builds the software CoreWeave uses to plan and operate its own infrastructure business. Some of that is UNION, our data platform, where anyone in the company can query the lakehouse in plain language and stand up their own dashboards, applications, and agents. The rest is the applications behind decisions like which data centers get which hardware and when, for a company adding gigawatts of capacity a year. Engineering, finance, supply chain, and data center operations all depend on what we ship.

You will ship features in UNION and in the applications teams run their processes on, working across the stack: TypeScript with React and Next.js in the browser, Python services running on Kubernetes, and the queries and data models underneath. Some of it is AI-facing, like the natural language interfaces and agents people use to ask questions against governed data. You will take one scoped piece at a time and carry it to production yourself, tests and post-release fixes included, working next to a senior engineer who owns the wider area. The people using it work here, so you will hear from them directly and see your work change how they work within a week or two.

Working proficiency in a backend language, Python preferred, and in JavaScript or TypeScript
Experience building web frontends with a modern framework such as React or Next.js
Experience building or consuming HTTP APIs in something that ran in production
Working SQL, including writing and debugging joins and aggregations against a relational database
Some exposure to AI and LLM development, such as prompting, retrieval, tool calling, or agents
Familiar with version control, code review, automated testing, and CI/CD

Experience building internal tools that other people relied on day to day

What Will You Do?
The Overview
The Site Reliability Engineer will ensure that Prolaio’s cardiovascular data platform reliably captures, transports, and delivers continuous biosensor data from participants to the clinical researchers and trial sponsors who depend on it. In this role, you will build and operate the monitoring, service level objectives, incident response, and automation needed to keep critical data flows healthy, identify failures before they impact studies, and ensure that device downtime never goes unnoticed simply because a shipment record says a device was delivered.
This role is ideal for a self-starter who thrives at the intersection of software reliability, connected devices, and clinical data. You will investigate incidents across the full participant-to-platform stack, combining service telemetry with device data and participant reports to determine whether an issue originated with the hardware, phone, firmware, mobile application, connectivity, or the platform itself. Build monitoring that treats missing data as a failure rather than a quiet day — freshness, volume and quality checks that verify delivery from outside the system instead of trusting a job's exit code.

Treat the fleet as a population — failure rates per device-month, clustering by build lot, firmware version or site — rather than as a queue of individual tickets.
Close the loop. When an analysis cannot reach a verdict, name the missing metric or threshold and route it back into the diagnostics pipeline so the next case is answerable from telemetry alone.
Build reliability tooling in Python and SQL on BigQuery, and keep monitors and probes defined as code rather than configured by hand.
Retire manual checks by automating them. Operational toil should shrink quarter over quarter, not accumulate.

Turn ideas, customer problems, and hypotheses into working prototypes, starting with our mobile app.

Create realistic customer simulations that can be tested with internal and external audiences.
Explore how to ground, guide, and evaluate AI experiences using customer profile data, customer context, and human-defined guardrails.
Connect prototypes to content libraries, AI SDKs, and staging systems.

Hands-on experience integrating and applying AI technologies, models, or services within applications, prototypes, or customer experiences.
Experience working with applied AI technologies such as LLMs, conversational AI, recommendation or decisioning systems, personalization, retrieval/grounding, agents, or generative AI.
Demonstrated ability to independently take an ambiguous AI-powered concept, determine how to build it, and deliver a functional POC or prototype.
Strong ability to move from an ambiguous idea or design concept to working software quickly.

Portfolio, prototypes, side projects, or examples that demonstrate curiosity and self-directed building.

Job Description
AI Automation Engineer
Must Have Technical/Functional Skills
3+ years of software engineering experience, with solid proficiency in Python and/or Node.js/TypeScript.

Strong written communication — comfortable working directly with an executive office to scope fast-turnaround, judgment-sensitive asks.

Prior work on an internal AI/automation platform team, or with a skills/plugin/tool registry and its certification pipeline.

Build and maintain Claude Skills/Plugins for Strategy, Portfolio and Governance's recurring deliverables: CW/vendor cost-split analysis (SOW-level 4 by support tier, supplier reconciliation to source-of-truth totals), org-change one-pagers, MPR pre-read assembly, AI-adoption reporting, and hiring job description generation.

title: Product Engineer
reason: Stack +43; Title fit +6; Exp fit +6; US +10; H1B +8; Senior salary -45
description_preview:
As Swing's Product Engineer, you'll find the problems worth solving across our business, decide what to build, and build it, reporting to the VP of Engineering. This isn't a traditional engineering seat: there's no PM → Designer → Engineer handoff, and you'll work directly with Product, Operations, Customer Success, Sales, and Finance to take problems from first conversation to shipped software. You'll build full-stack features for school administrators and substitute teachers, the operational systems that run our marketplace, and the automations and AI agents that replace manual work. AI is central to how you work, not just what you ship, and the role is designed so one person with the right tools can do what used to take a team. If you want to own problems end to end and see your work keep students learning, keep reading.
Keys to Success in This Role
Full-stack engineering with a shipping record:
You have 3+ years of software engineering or equivalent hands-on product building, and you've shipped real products that customers use. Here you'll work across the stack, from features school administrators and subs use every day to billing, timekeeping, configuration, integrations, and admin tools.
An AI-native way of working:
Tools like Claude Code, n8n, and other AI and automation tools are the core of your workflow, and you keep experimenting to increase your leverage. You'll be expected to turn an idea into something users can interact with in hours or days, not weeks.
Product judgment:
You ask why before deciding how. Without waiting on a PM, you'll define requirements, set scope, make UX and product tradeoffs, and decide when something is ready to ship.
Turning ambiguity into working software:
Problems will reach you loosely defined, from teams across the business. You dig in, work out what's actually needed, and build a solution that works.
Automating operations:
You spot repetitive manual workflows and replace them with software, AI agents, APIs, MCP, or tools like n8n. Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs, agents, or AI-powered workflows is what lets you do this well.
Clear communication and measurable results:
You explain tradeoffs plainly to non-technical teammates and in depth to engineers, collaborating during U.S. business hours. You use data and user feedback to show whether what you built actually solved the problem.
Founder or early-startup experience is a plus:
Having built a product or startup yourself, been an early engineer, or taken on PM responsibilities will help you hit the ground running. So will examples where AI let you accomplish what previously required several people.
What You'll Work With
You'll need hands-on experience with React for building user interfaces in JavaScript or TypeScript, working with REST APIs to connect systems, and using SQL and relational databases to query and shape data. Those are the core of the stack you'll touch every day.
Experience with any of these will let you move faster: Clojure or another Lisp, since much of our backend is Clojure; Datomic, the database we use for our core application data; AWS infrastructure, where our systems run; or building browser extensions, which we use to extend third-party platforms our customers rely on. If you haven't worked with these, you'll pick them up as you go.
Why You're Excited About This Job
The mission:
The average student spends six months of their K-12 career with a substitute teacher. What you build helps schools get coverage quickly and keeps student learning on track.
End-to-end ownership:
You decide what to build, build it, and measure whether it worked. No handoffs, no waiting on a spec.
A mandate to define AI-native work:
We're rethinking how we build products and run the business in an AI-native world, and you'll help shape what that looks like at Swing.
Leverage by design:
This role is built around the idea that AI lets one person accomplish what once took a team, and you'll push that idea as far as it goes.
The full inside of a marketplace:
You'll build for both sides of a two-sided marketplace and for its operational core: billing, timekeeping, integrations, and admin tools.
Cross-functional exposure:
You'll partner directly with Product, Operations, Customer Success, Sales, and Finance, and see the business from every seat.
Visible impact:
Every workflow you automate and every feature you ship changes how our team and our customers work, and you'll have the data to prove it.
About Swing Education
Swing Education is an online staffing marketplace that connects substitute teachers with K-12 schools. Founded in 2015 by former K-12 educators and administrators, Swing makes it easier for schools and districts to find reliable, qualified substitute teachers when they need them most. We recruit, screen, and support a large community of substitute teachers, and we build technology that helps schools get coverage quickly.
We believe substitute teachers play an integral role in education; the average student spends six months of their K-12 time with a sub. With millions of absence days filled to date, we're dedicated to improving the experience of finding substitute teachers, becoming a sub, and keeping student learning on track.
--
Swing Education is unable to provide employment visa sponsorship, including H-1B sponsorship, for this position. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without current or future sponsorship.
Salary is commensurate on experience and is adjusted for cost of living standards dependent on position location. Swing Education offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes the following perks:Medical/dental/vision benefitsFlexible Time Off (FTO)Paid holidaysParental leaveStock optionsProfessional development reimbursement programCo-working membership reimbursementMission-driven workFun, collaborative, balanced culture
COMPENSATION:: $110,000 USD - $130,000 USD

About the Role
This is an early-career role designed for a new or recent graduate who is excited to build a career in applied AI. You'll join our Data & Analytics team and work alongside experienced engineers and external delivery partners to help design, build, and support AI-powered solutions — including chat assistants, workflow automation, and integrations with our business systems.
You won't be expected to know everything on day one. We'll invest in your growth through mentorship, hands-on projects, code reviews, and structured onboarding. What matters most is a solid foundation in programming and AI concepts, genuine curiosity, and the drive to learn quickly. If you've built things in school, an internship, a bootcamp, or on your own — and you're eager to do it in a production environment with people who will help you level up — we'd like to hear from you.
What You'll Do
You'll start with well-scoped tasks and grow toward more independent work as you develop. Day to day, you will:
Help translate product requirements and user stories into AI/ML solutions, with guidance from senior engineers and the Product Manager
Contribute to building and testing AI chat assistants and automation tools for internal teams, in collaboration with senior engineers and external partners
Assist in integrating AI solutions with existing databases, APIs, and business applications
Help build, train, and evaluate machine-learning and LLM-based features, learning our production, quality, and security standards as you go
Contribute to agentic and retrieval-augmented (RAG) workflows using frameworks such as LangChain or similar — beginning with guided tasks and building toward independence
Support and help maintain existing AI agents, tools, and automations, including troubleshooting with support from the team
Write clean, well-documented code and take part in code reviews to build strong engineering habits
Help support and promote our internal AI chat platform (WPChat) across the organization
Document what you build, and stay current with AI/ML developments — sharing what you learn with the team
Collaborate across IT, data, and business teams, and partner with external vendors on delivery
How You'll Grow — What You'll Learn Here
These are skills you'll
develop on the job
with mentorship — not prerequisites. Over roughly your first 6–18 months, you can expect to gain hands-on, production experience with:
Agent orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, or AutoGen) and patterns such as ReAct and plan-and-execute, including memory and human-in-the-loop flows
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and NLP tooling — e.g., LlamaIndex, Haystack, PyTorch, scikit-learn
Deploying AI solutions on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and platform tools such as Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, or Azure AI Foundry
Working with AI gateways (e.g., Portkey, Kong) and MCP servers that connect to enterprise systems (Oracle, Workday, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Jira)
Building and integrating RPA workflows and connecting them to LLM decision layers
MLOps practices for deploying and monitoring models, and building conversational AI across channels (web chat, and potentially voice, SMS, and email)
What We're Looking For
The essentials — this is what we actually require:
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field — or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience (including bootcamps or a strong self-taught portfolio). Recent and upcoming graduates are welcome.
Foundational programming ability in Python, demonstrated through coursework, internships, academic or personal projects, bootcamp work, or open-source contributions
A working understanding of core AI/ML and large language model (LLM) concepts — how they work and where they're used — from classes, projects, or self-study
Hands-on exposure to at least one area relevant to the role: building something with an LLM or an AI framework (e.g., LangChain), a machine-learning project, an API integration, or a chatbot. A class, capstone, or personal project counts.
Comfort with engineering fundamentals: version control (Git), reading documentation, and debugging
Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a genuine eagerness to learn
Clear communication and a collaborative, team-oriented mindset
Nice to Have (Bonus, Not Required)
Any of these will strengthen your application, but none are expected of an early-career candidate:
Any hands-on exposure to LLM agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, LangGraph, CrewAI, Flowise) or RAG tools (LlamaIndex, Haystack)
Any experience with a cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP) or an AI platform tool (Vertex AI, Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry)
Exposure to LibreChat, MLOps tooling, AI gateways (Portkey, Kong), or MCP servers
Coursework or projects in NLP, chatbots, or conversational AI (including voice, SMS, email, or web chat)
Any internship or project experience, including in web, eCommerce, or general software development
Familiarity with data privacy and security basics
Interest in or exposure to the wholesale distribution, manufacturing, CPG, or eCommerce industries

This is a full-time, on-site position at our Oak Brook, IL office. You'll be part of a team that's invested in your development.
